persona.who: 29, chartered accountant in Indore, married 1 year, lives with in-laws who expect her to give up the practice after a baby. Husband avoids the topic.
persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told you will disappear after your baby is born to standing in the life you built and the man you married.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being told you will be erased, and the anger of your husband's silence, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built her CA practice from zero is being told by her mother-in-law she will leave work after her baby is born, while her husband stays silent.
understanding.mirror: You built this practice from nothing, and now you're being told it will end the moment your baby is born.
understanding.insight: The baby they speak of is not yet born, but the life they say will disappear is the one you built with your own hands, and that is what is being erased.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being told the life you built will end the moment your baby is born, and the anger of watching your own husband stay silent while it happens.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her husband's family and left alone by her husband, who questioned them and stood in her truth.

verse.speaker: Sita
verse.setting: After the war, Ram publicly voices suspicion of Sita; she answers his harsh words before the assembly.
verse.sanskrit: सह संवृद्धभावेन संसर्गेण च मानद। यदि तेऽहं न विज्ञाता हता तेनास्मि शाश्वतम्॥
verse.line: After all these years together, if you still don't know me, that loss is forever.
verse.translation: We grew up together in love and lived together so long. If even so you have not understood me, then I am lost forever.
verse.why: Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice; you are allowed to name it.
verse.misuse: This is Sita's protest against unjust suspicion; the app does not endorse the test that follows.

prasang.title: Sita answers unjust suspicion
prasang.summary: After the war Ram publicly doubts Sita. She answers with dignity: why speak to me like a stranger? After all our years together, if you don't know me, that loss is permanent. She then walks into fire to prove what should not have needed proof.
prasang.lesson: Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice; you are allowed to name it.

verse.meaning: After the war, Ram publicly voices doubt about Sita's purity before the entire court. Sita, who has already suffered enough, answers him with a quiet, devastating truth. She reminds him that they grew up together in love, that they lived together for so long. If even after all that time he still does not know her, then that loss is forever. She is not asking for proof. She is naming the deep injustice of being doubted by someone who is supposed to know her best.
verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
verse.sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
verse.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
verse.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verse.why: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

prasang.title: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.
prasang.story_hook: Mandodari took her husband's hand and led him somewhere the ministers couldn't hear.
prasang.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

verse.meaning: Tulsidas speaks this in the Ramcharitmanas as Ravana's ministers flatter their king while the enemy army waits at the gates. The poet notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed. The verse proposes that ruin comes quickly when a circle of yes-men replaces honest counsel. It turns gently toward the life you are building, where the voices around you could match the truth of your work.
verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi says this to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata as they sit in the forest. She argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act. The verse proposes that a person should never look down on themselves. The one who despises themselves never finds real prosperity. It turns gently toward your situation, where the work you have built is already real.
verse.for_you: Your self-worth is not a feeling to be earned by their approval. It is the ground beneath the practice you built from zero. Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying on the ground, defeated and refusing to rise after losing his kingdom. She tells him to stop holding himself in contempt. She says he must set his mind on what is truly good and pull himself together. She does not promise him the kingdom back. She simply tells him that past failure does not define him and that those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: The life you built is not gone because it is not yet born. The baby does not erase the years you spent building your practice. Hold to that work as your mind, and let it steady you while the silence around you continues.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is speaking to Nidagha about how a person who has found freedom moves through the world. He tells him to do the work in front of him, to speak gently, to read what is in people's hearts, and not to sink. This means you live fully in the world, doing what comes, while staying calm and unhurried on the inside. You let go of what is lost and take up what is there. You do not grieve or crave. You speak what is agreeable to all, and you know the intent of others.
verse.for_you: The work in front of you is your CA practice and the man you married. Do it. Speak gently to your mother-in-law, but read her heart. She wants to erase you, but you will not sink. You are building a life, and you will stay afloat.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna about what real effort looks like, not the kind done for show. He says that speech is a form of discipline, and the right kind is words that do not wound, that are true, kind and helpful. This is not about being polite to avoid conflict. It is about speaking with a steady heart, saying what is needed without cruelty, and letting the truth stand on its own. What comes next in the story is that effort and giving also have three kinds, and the showy kind does not last.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.

story.title: Queen Chudala teaches her husband what renunciation really is
story.story_hook: The queen had found peace, and the king, who loved her, could not believe it.
story.summary: Queen Chudala finds inner peace, but her husband, King Shikhidhvaja, doesn't believe her. Restless, he leaves his kingdom for the forest. Chudala rules wisely in his absence and visits him disguised as a young sage, Kumbha, who shows him that giving up kingdom, home and body is not renunciation; letting go of the clinging mind is. Freed, he returns home and rules beside her.
story.lesson: Running away doesn't free you; letting go inside does. Sometimes the teacher is the person beside you.

anchor.speaker: Kumbha (Queen Chudala in disguise)
anchor.setting: Queen Chudala, disguised as the young sage Kumbha, visits her husband who fled to the forest.
anchor.sanskrit: साधो न देहत्यागेन न राज्यत्यजनेन च । न चोटजादिशोषेण सर्वत्यागो भवेन्नृप ॥
anchor.line: Giving up your kingdom, your body, or living in a hut won't free you. Real letting go is inside.
anchor.translation: Good man, true renunciation does not come from giving up the body, nor from giving up the kingdom, nor from wasting away in a hut, O king.
anchor.why: Running away doesn't free you; letting go inside does. Sometimes the teacher is the person beside you.
anchor.misuse: Not 'never change your life'. It says outer escape without inner change doesn't work.

script: You feel erased and unsupported, and you are right to. Someone is telling you that the life you built with your own hands will vanish the moment your baby arrives. They are looking at you as if you are less than you are.
After the war, Ram stands before the entire court. He voices a public doubt about Sita. Sita, who has already suffered enough, looks at him and speaks a quiet, devastating truth. Sita said:
सह संवृद्धभावेन संसर्गेण च मानद, यदि तेऽहं न विज्ञाता हता तेनास्मि शाश्वतम्.
In plain words: After all these years together, if you still don't know me, that loss is forever.

Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice, and you are allowed to name it. This is easier said than done, because you are expected to absorb the hurt silently. But the truth underneath is that their inability to see you does not make you smaller. It makes their sight the thing that is broken.
Look at the woman who built your CA practice from zero. She is not a guest in your home. She is the architect of the life you two are building. Let her stand in that truth today.
What they see is not who you are.

depth.life: Your mother-in-law is already erasing the CA practice you built from nothing. Your husband stays quiet, and the silence makes you feel erased and unsupported. You are carrying the weight of a future that has not even arrived, and it feels like the life you built is being treated as worthless before it has even begun.
depth.points: Being doubted by someone close is a deep injustice. It is not a misunderstanding. It is a refusal to see you. You are allowed to name it. Your worth was never theirs to grant or take away.
depth.practice: Look at the phone and name one thing you know about yourself that they do not see.
depth.question: What would it cost you to name this loss out loud?
